coverage.value: Evangelical Baptist Missions — ebm.org — MISS. site:ebm.org returns nothing owned by an independent Baptist US sending agency; results are hijacked by ebm-international.org (EBM International, the German Baptist union agency) and by Wikipedia. A Christian Post article, 'Evangelical Baptist Mission Undone by Poor Financial Decisions', indicates the US agency is defunct. No missionary surface of any kind on ebm.org. Do not re-probe.

Baptist Bible Fellowship International — bbfi.org — MISS on this domain. bbfi.org is the fellowship/association site (about-the-bbfi, contact-us, events, articles-of-faith, central-office). No /missionaries path, no per-person pages. The missionary surface lives on a SEPARATE domain, bbfimissions.com.

Baptist Bible Fellowship International Mission Office — bbfimissions.com — HIT, and the biggest one in this slice. Per-person pages at bbfimissions.com/missionary/<slug>. The domain uses TWO slug shapes interchangeably: 'first-and-first-surname' (nolan-and-janay-letourneau, mike-and-cindy-burgett, james-and-amy-smith) and 'surname-first-and-first' (wyatt-michael-and-cristy). Page titles are 'First and First Surname - Baptist Bible Fellowship International'. Roster hub at bbfimissions.com/missionaries with a ?show=all variant. Org states 700+ missionaries in 80+ nations, so this domain is far from exhausted and deserves a dedicated full-budget wave. Related subdomains: thebridge.bbfimissions.com (news/editorial, includes obituaries and 'Heroes of the Faith' memorials — hazardous) and donate.bbfimissions.com (project pages, not people).

Baptist International Outreach — biomissions.org — HIT, but weakly indexed. Per-person pages sit at the ROOT of the domain: biomissions.org/david-and-stephanie-peach/, biomissions.org/frank-laurent/. Roster at biomissions.org/missionaries/ lists everyone 'Surname, First and First — Country/City'. Org self-reports 100+ American missionaries plus 50+ nationals in 20+ countries, and a 2016 figure of 57 families / 107 missionaries. Problem for search-only mining: the site is a WordPress blog and the index is dominated by 'Into All the World' newsletter issues, prayer-letter posts and tag archives, which crowd out the profile pages. A fetch pass on biomissions.org/missionaries/ would convert the whole roster in one hit. Also noted: missionary.biomissions.org is a login-gated missionary portal.

Baptist Faith Missions — bfmnow.org (not the guessed baptistfaithmissions.org) — PARTIAL. Roster at bfmnow.org/missionaries/ names couples in full with fields. There are NO per-person profile slugs; per-person content is served as WordPress TAG ARCHIVES (bfmnow.org/tag/darrell-messer/, /tag/bobby-creiglow/, /tag/peru-missionaries/). Tag slugs do carry full names, so they are citable at medium but are not profile pages with a support ask. Small agency — self-describes as seven missionary families in Brazil, Peru, France and Kenya — so ceiling is roughly 14 adults. Archive holds decades of Mission Sheets PDFs naming long-dead missionaries; heavy death risk if mined by name alone.

needs_review.issue: Deceased spouse — do not emit either name without a fresh check
needs_review.finding: Ken and Louise Board, BBFI missionaries to Japan from 1968. Louise Board died of a cerebral hemorrhage in Japan after 41 years of missionary service.
needs_review.evidence: https://thebridge.bbfimissions.com/heroes-of-the-faith-ken-louise-board/ — a 'Heroes of the Faith' memorial article, not a profile page. The article also names their children Timothy, Rebecca, Merri and Tabitha, who are out of scope as children.
needs_review.recommendation: Emit neither. Ken Board's current status and whether he still holds active missionary status are unknown. If a bbfimissions.com/missionary/ slug exists for the couple, check its TITLE before touching it — this domain is exactly the memorial-rewrite hazard the brief warns about.

needs_review.issue: Deceased missionary named in an obituary post
needs_review.finding: Nancy Mantonya, BBFI missionary to Brazil (approved with husband Henry in May 1971), has died. Henry Mantonya is the surviving spouse. Their son James and daughter Jayme (Radak) are described as also serving as BBFI missionaries to Brazil.
needs_review.recommendation: Never emit Nancy Mantonya. Henry Mantonya may be emittable but only from a live per-person page whose title names him. James Mantonya and Jayme Radak appear to be adult missionaries in their own right, not dependents, but no per-person URL was found for either — resolve with a targeted bbfimissions.com/missionary/ lookup before emitting.

needs_review.finding: Dan and Sharon Moore appear under BBFI's 'Heroes of the Faith' series, the same series that carried the Ken and Louise Board memorial.
needs_review.recommendation: Treat the entire 'Heroes of the Faith' series on thebridge.bbfimissions.com as a death/retirement flag, not a lead source. Do not emit from it.

needs_review.finding: 'Christine', reinstated to active BBFI missionary status for Kenya in September 2024, is named with no surname in the source. 'The Pattersons' (Philippines, Aeta ministry) and 'The Allreds' (Merida, Mexico) appear as family names with no first names.

needs_review.issue: Generational name collision with high death risk
needs_review.finding: Baptist Faith Missions has both a 'Bobby Creiglow' tag archive and references to Mike and Beverly Creiglow in Brazil. BFM is a multi-generational agency (the Hatchers are explicitly 'third generation') and its site hosts Mission Sheets newsletter PDFs back to at least 1984.
needs_review.recommendation: Do not emit Bobby Creiglow — a tag archive on a site with 40 years of back issues gives no evidence the person is living or active. Mike and Beverly Creiglow were NOT emitted for the same reason: the only attribution was a newsletter reference, not the current roster. Any BFM mining must read bfmnow.org/missionaries/ directly and treat tag archives as history, not roster.

needs_review.finding: Yohannes and Kidist Getaneh (Zambia, Deaf church planting, credited with helping start 25 Deaf churches) and Tesfaye and Alemitu Gosa (Ethiopia) are described in BIO's own material. BIO states it has 50+ national missionaries alongside its 100+ American missionaries.
needs_review.recommendation: Not emitted. These appear in BIO's narrative pages rather than in a quoted roster line, and nationals supported through BIO's fund-processing may sit outside the Tier A deputation model. Confirm against the roster before emitting; if emitted, note the national-missionary distinction.

needs_review.issue: Roster pages that would convert in a single fetch
needs_review.finding: Three roster pages name every missionary in full but resist search-only enumeration because the surrounding blog content dominates the index.
needs_review.evidence: https://bbfimissions.com/missionaries?show=all (the ?show=all variant is the whole list on one page), https://biomissions.org/missionaries/, https://www.bfmnow.org/missionaries/
needs_review.recommendation: Queue all three for a fetch pass. bbfimissions.com/missionaries?show=all is the single highest-value URL found in this slice — 700+ support-raising adults behind one request, with confirmed per-person pages to cite for each.
